questions.q: What is the key difference between an estimated plan and an actual plan?
options: The estimated plan is compiled from statistics without running the query; the actual plan requires execution and includes real row counts and (2016+) per-operator time
They are always identical for every query
The actual plan is only available in Azure SQL Database
The estimated plan shows real row counts, and the actual plan does not
questions.explain: Estimated plans are compile-time predictions; actual plans come from running the query and expose the real numbers the estimate was tested against.

questions.q: What does SET STATISTICS XML ON produce?
options: The actual execution plan as XML — the same underlying data SSMS's graphical actual-plan view uses
A list of all statistics objects on a database
A count of how many indexes exist on a table
A plain-text summary with no plan information at all
questions.explain: STATISTICS XML captures the actual plan in XML form, which is the same data source SSMS's graphical actual plan view renders from.

questions.q: Why is a large gap between Estimated Number of Rows and Actual Number of Rows on an operator significant?
options: It means the optimizer built its entire plan (join type, index choice, parallelism) around a wrong picture of the data, making everything downstream of that operator suspect
It means the query returned no rows at all
It is always caused by a hardware failure
It has no diagnostic value and can be ignored
questions.explain: The optimizer's decisions are all made based on its row-count estimate; when that estimate is far off from reality, its downstream choices may be wrong too.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what are the two most likely root causes of a large estimated-vs-actual row count mismatch?
options: Stale statistics, or parameter sniffing
A missing backup and a corrupted log file
Too much available memory and too few CPU cores
An outdated version of SSMS
questions.explain: The lesson names stale statistics (outdated histogram) and parameter sniffing (plan compiled for an atypical parameter value) as the two usual causes.

questions.q: Why does it matter whether a mismatch is caused by stale statistics versus parameter sniffing?
options: The fixes are different — stale stats is resolved once for everyone via UPDATE STATISTICS, while parameter sniffing needs a plan-shape or compilation strategy fix even when statistics are already current
There is no practical difference; both are fixed the same way
Parameter sniffing can only happen on stale statistics, never on current ones
Stale statistics can only be fixed by rebuilding all indexes on the server
questions.explain: Because the underlying cause is different, the correct remedy differs too — updating stats doesn't help a parameter-sniffing case where stats are already accurate.
